edits.hypothesis: Detecting silent tool failures (status=completed but observation=None) and converting them to explicit failures forces the agent to acknowledge the missing evidence rather than proceeding as if the tool succeeded or was unnecessary.
edits.why_not_lower_lever: A prompt edit cannot reliably prevent the agent from hallucinating that a planned tool call executed when the environment provides no feedback; the control flow must explicitly flag the missing observation as a failure state.
edits.trigger_condition: When a tool call returns status 'completed' but observation is None and no failure_observation is present.
edits.retroactive_check: (corrective) In q000009, the roi_crop call returned no observation. The new logic would mark it as failed, triggering delivered_failure which instructs the agent to continue from original images and not repeat the call. This prevents the agent from ignoring the missing crop and relying solely on the negative LLaVA-Med output. (preservative) Successful tool calls with valid observations are unaffected. (transfer) Generalizes to any tool that might silently fail to return data without an explicit error status.
edits.regression_risk: Low. Only affects cases where observation is strictly None despite completed status, which is currently a bug/edge case leading to incorrect behavior.
edits.mechanism: Detecting silent tool failures (status=completed but observation=None) and converting them to explicit failures forces the agent to acknowledge the missing evidence rather than proceeding as if the tool succeeded or was unnecessary.

mechanism: Add silent-failure detection in executor to convert missing-observation tool calls into explicit failures, preventing the agent from ignoring unexecuted tool plans.
